facts.statement: The only known species of Huallasaurus is H. australis.
facts.quote: The type and only species is H. australis.

facts.statement: Originally described in 1984 as a species of Kritosaurus, Huallasaurus was recognized as a distinct genus separate from Secernosaurus and other Kritosaurini members in a 2022 study.
facts.quote: Originally named as a species of Kritosaurus in 1984, it was long considered a synonym of Secernosaurus before being recognized as its own distinct genus in a 2022 study, different from other members of Kritosaurini.

facts.statement: The genus name Huallasaurus combines the Mapudungun word for duck and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, "Huallasaurus," combines "hualla," the Mapudungun word for "duck," and the Greek "sauros," meaning "lizard."

facts.statement: The species name australis means southern, referring to the location of the holotype specimen in southern Argentina.
facts.quote: The specific name, "australis," is derived from the Latin "australis," meaning "southern," after the discovery of the holotype specimen in southern Argentina.

facts.statement: Rozadilla et al. (2022) recovered Huallasaurus within a clade consisting entirely of South American saurolophines.
facts.quote: Rozadilla et al. (2022) named Huallasaurus and the closely related Kelumapusaura, recovering them in a clade of entirely South American saurolophines.

facts.statement: The clade containing Huallasaurus and other South American saurolophines was named Austrokritosauria and is recovered as the sister taxon to Kritosaurini.
facts.quote: They named the clade containing Huallasaurus, Kelumapusaura, and other South American saurolophines as the Austrokritosauria, recovering it as the sister taxon to the Kritosaurini.

facts.statement: Huallasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 73 and 69 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 73 y 69 durante el Campaniense y el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Huallasaurus is estimated to have reached a length of around 8 meters.
facts.quote: Se calcula que llegó a medir alrededor de 8 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The species was originally named in 1984 from Late Campanian to Early Maastrichtian fossils found in the Los Alamitos Formation of Río Negro Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: En 1984, el paleontólogo argentino José Fernando Bonaparte y colegas nombraron K. australis a huesos de un hadrosáurido de finales del Campaniano a principios del Maastrichiano, proveniente de la Formación Los Alamitos de la Provincia del Río Negro, Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: While previously considered a synonym of Secernosaurus koerneri, new evidence in 2022 recognized "Kritosaurus" australis as a valid taxon distinct from other South American hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Estudios posteriores colocaron esta especie es un sinónimo más moderno de Secernosaurus koerneri, pero seguía siendo problemático. En 2022 nueva evidencia nos permite reconocer que Secernosaurus koerneri, Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis y "Kritosaurus" australis son taxones válidos.

facts.statement: Huallasaurus was proposed as a new genus name for the species "Kritosaurus" australis to distinguish it from other South American taxa and North American Kritosaurus.
facts.quote: Este último se puede distinguir de los otros taxones sudamericanos, así como de Kritosaurus de América del Norte, por lo que se propuso Huallasaurus como un nuevo nombre genérico para la especie "Kritosaurus" australis.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovers a new clade of South American hadrosaurs composed of Kelumapusaura machi, Huallasaurus australis, Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis, and Secernosaurus koerneri.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético recupera un nuevo clado de hadrosáuridos sudamericanos compuesto por Kelumapusaura machi, Huallasaurus australis, Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis y Secernosaurus koerneri.

facts.statement: The new South American clade is tentatively nested between Kritosaurini and is supported by traits including a subhorizontal crest on the ilium, a longitudinal crest on the dorsal surface of the postacetabular process, and a twisted distal end of the postacetabular process.
facts.quote: El nuevo clado sudamericano está tentativamente anidado entre Kritosaurini y está respaldado por varios rasgos, incluido un ilion con una cresta subhorizontal que separa la muesca preacetabular del pedículo púbico, una cresta longitudinal en la superficie dorsal del proceso postacetabular, y un extremo distal torcido del proceso postacetabular.

facts.statement: The recovery of a monophyletic clade of South American hadrosaurs indicates that the history of hadrosaurs on Gondwanan landmasses is poorly understood, and new discoveries may alter current views on their taxonomy and phylogenetic relationships.
facts.quote: La recuperación de un clado monofilético de hadrosáuridos sudamericanos indica que la historia de los hadrosáuridos en las masas terrestres de Gondwana está lejos de comprenderse bien, y los nuevos descubrimientos pueden cambiar la imagen actual de la taxonomía y las relaciones filogenéticas de los dinosaurios de pico de pato del sur.

facts.statement: Huallasaurus belongs to the parent group Kritosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Kritosaurini

facts.statement: Huallasaurus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Huallasaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: CT scans revealed that Huallasaurus vertebrae had a relatively dense trabecular architecture and lacked invasive pneumaticity in the centra, neural arches, and neural spines.
facts.quote: It was found that the internal structure had a relatively dense trabecular architecture and a lack of invasive pneumaticity across the centra, neural arches, and neural spines.

facts.statement: The internal vertebral structure of Huallasaurus is more similar to silesaurs like Silesaurus than to other archosauriforms.
facts.quote: The internal pattern is more similar to silesaurs (such as Silesaurus) more than that of other archosauriforms.

facts.statement: It is currently debated whether the similarity in vertebral structure between Huallasaurus and silesaurs indicates a deep phylogenetic relationship or convergent evolution.
facts.quote: It is currently an open question weather these similarity show a deep phylogenetic relationship or convergent evolutions between the groups.

facts.statement: The lack of invasive air sacs in Huallasaurus vertebrae supports the hypothesis that air sac diverticula did not evolve in Ornithischia and suggests a "pelvic bellows" ventilation mechanism.
facts.quote: It seems that these observations are consistent with the hypothesis that the air sac diverticula did not evolve in the clade Ornithischia and instead supports the proposed "pelvic bellows" ventilation hypothesis.

facts.statement: Huallasaurus may have supported its large body size and fat reserves through a combination of dense trabecular bone, thin cortical walls, and the absence of invasive air sacs.
facts.quote: Their large body sizes and accommodated intraosseous fat reserves may have been supported by a combination of a dense trabecular matrix and thin cortical walls and the lack of invasive air sacs.

facts.statement: While Huallasaurus vertebrae superficially resemble those of large mammals with expanded trabecular matrices and thin walls, the functional equivalence of these structures is speculative.
facts.quote: They also show superficial similarities to the trabecular structure that are seen in some large mammal species with their expanded trabecular matrix and remarkably thin cortical walls. However their functional equivalence is speculative.

facts.statement: Huallasaurus fossils are known from the Late Cretaceous Los Alamitos Formation of Río Negro Province, Argentina, where the sauropod Aeolosaurus rionegrinus has also been found.
facts.quote: Huallasaurus is known from the Late Cretaceous Los Alamitos Formation of Río Negro Province, Argentina. Aeolosaurus rionegrinus, a titanosaurian sauropod, has also been named from this formation.

rejected.statement: Huallasaurus is an extinct genus of saurolophine hadrosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia, Argentina.
rejected.quote: Huallasaurus (meaning "duck lizard") is an extinct genus of saurolophine hadrosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous of the Los Alamitos Formation of Patagonia in Argentina.
